projects_section.title: Projects
projects_section.intro: LLM applications in production, validated machine learning and biomedical data analysis.

items.title: Job Matcher: AI job application assistant
items.challenge: Generic AI tools invent experience and give inconsistent advice. I wanted an assistant whose recommendations can be trusted and explained.
items.approach: Hybrid architecture. Gemini extracts the offer's requirements with structured output; filtering, match percentage and the final recommendation are deterministic code that is explainable and testable.
items.result: I chose the model with an evaluation on 20 real job offers reviewed by hand: correct requirements went from 82/140 to 97/140 (59% → 69%) with no recommendation changed.
items.story: Multi-user web app that I designed, built and deployed. It analyses job offers in 5+ languages and generates tailored CVs and cover letters without inventing data.
items.production_note: Job Matcher runs in production at lab.asansal.com, where I publish my personal projects.
impact: Validators check figures, references and skills against hallucinations and retry automatically.
RAG with Google Search grounding and cited sources for market research, company notes and learning plans, with a shared cache.
About 3 LLM calls per full application, with per-user quotas and cost logging.

items.title: Sextant IA
items.challenge: Planning a tailor-made trip takes hours of research and rarely includes the historical or cultural context of each place.
items.approach: Multi-stage pipeline with the Google Gemini API (Flash or Pro per stage). A prompt engine splits the work into discovery, day-by-day skeleton, daily plans, accommodation and details, with chained and parallel calls (ThreadPoolExecutor). Human-in-the-loop: the user picks among the discovery proposals before the full trip is generated.
items.result: Full Django app (views, sessions, models, admin, tests), background tasks with a progress page, PDF export (ReportLab), maps and LLM-based translation into 8 languages.
items.story: Solo project, 245 commits since February 2026. It combines two interests of mine: travel and history.
items.production_note: Sextant IA is published and running in production at sextantia.eu.
impact: Structured JSON output with a 7-step repair process, per-model timeouts, retries and detection of orphaned tasks.
Own server on Oracle Cloud (Gunicorn, Nginx, Certbot, systemd, SELinux) with continuous deployment from GitHub Actions.
Privacy by design: no user accounts, no stored profiles, reCAPTCHA.

items.title: DSMarket: Retail Forecasting
items.type: Data Science & Business Intelligence · Master's capstone, team project
items.challenge: A chain with 3,049 products and 10 stores needed to anticipate weekly demand to plan stock.
items.approach: I owned the time-series forecasting. We prepared 5 years of sales (6.7 million rows, ~30,000 item-store series) with price, calendar, weather and event features, segmented products with K-Means, and compared Lasso and XGBoost with time-series cross-validation and Optuna.
items.result: The final Lasso model beat a naive last-week baseline by 10% (RMSE) and 13% (WMAPE) on a held-out 9-week test set, with a Power BI dashboard by region, store and segment. It was not deployed to production.

items.title: Clinical trial dashboard (R Shiny)
items.challenge: Quickly explore the results of a clinical trial by treatment arm and patient subgroup.
items.approach: Interactive dashboard on a simulated 500-patient, three-arm trial (placebo, drug A and B): treatment and gender filters, KPIs and biomarker response charts, built with Shiny modules and custom CSS.
items.result: App deployed on shinyapps.io. The data are simulated and do not represent real patients.

items.title: Leishmania genome re-annotation with Ribo-Seq
items.challenge: The Leishmania donovani genome annotation missed regions that the parasite actually translates into protein.
items.approach: I designed and analysed Ribo-Seq experiments (ribosome-protected mRNA fragments) with Python and Bash scripts, parallelised with GNU Parallel, to detect translated reading frames.
items.result: Refined genome annotation, published in Genes (2023) as first author. DOI 10.3390/genes14081637.

items.title: Proteogenomics of Leishmania donovani
items.challenge: The Leishmania donovani reference genome did not capture every protein the parasite actually produces.
items.approach: I integrated mass spectrometry data with the genome annotation and statistically validated the candidate coding sequences.
items.result: Identification of previously unannotated proteins, published in Genes (2024). DOI 10.3390/genes15060775.

items.title: Environmental transcriptomics in aquatic ecosystems
items.challenge: Analysing microbial communities in nutrient-poor lakes produced more data than could be processed locally.
items.approach: I set up hybrid local/HPC workflows with Slurm to assemble transcriptomes de novo and applied multivariate statistics in R.
items.result: Complete community analysis while making the most of limited computing resources.

items.title: This portfolio: AI-assisted website with continuous deployment
items.challenge: I wanted a multilingual portfolio with an assistant that answers questions about my career and updates itself.
items.approach: Streamlit and a Google Gemini chatbot that answers from my own knowledge base. Linux server on Oracle Cloud, deployed with GitHub Actions on every push.
items.result: Production website in six languages, continuously deployed with no manual steps.

items.title: A Proteogenomic Approach to Unravel New Proteins Encoded in the Leishmania donovani (HU3) Genome
items.authors: J. Adán-Jiménez, A. Sánchez-Salvador, E. Morato, J.C. Solana, B. Aguado, J.M. Requena
items.description: Integration of mass spectrometry with genomics and statistical validation of new coding sequences.
items.summary: Proteomics relies on accurate genome annotation: when genes or proteins are missing, part of the data is lost. Following a proteogenomic strategy, we generated mass spectrometry data from L. donovani (HU3 strain) promastigotes and detected 1,908 proteins using the public annotations. Searching the same data against every open reading frame in the genome let us annotate 20 new protein-coding genes and extend the N-terminal end of 43 proteins. We also found many post-translational modifications (phosphorylation, acetylation, methylation…) and, by comparing with the L. major proteome, showed how comparing proteomes only by their protein lists can lead to wrong conclusions.
highlights: 1,908 proteins detected in L. donovani promastigotes.
20 new protein-coding genes and 43 proteins extended at their N-terminal end.
Raw data on ProteomeXchange (PXD051920) and updated gene models in open repositories.
items.image_caption: (A) Mass spectra of peptides that extend the coding region of LdHU3_22.1300. (B) Alignment of that region with other Leishmania species.

items.title: Refinement of Leishmania donovani Genome Annotations in the Light of Ribosome-Protected mRNAs Fragments (Ribo-Seq Data)
items.authors: A. Sánchez-Salvador, S. González-de la Fuente, B. Aguado, P.A. Yates, J.M. Requena
items.description: First author. Ribo-Seq data analysis and custom scripts to detect translated open reading frames (ORFs).
items.summary: Automated genome annotation needs to be curated with functional data. We used public Ribo-Seq data, the sequencing of ribosome-protected mRNA fragments, to refine the annotation of the L. donovani (HU3 strain) genome. We uncovered 70 previously non-annotated protein-coding genes, improved the annotation of around 600 genes and found small upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in many transcripts, pointing to a role in translational regulation. The bioinformatics pipelines we developed can be applied to any organism with Ribo-Seq data.
highlights: Reusable bioinformatics pipelines for other organisms with Ribo-Seq data.
items.image_caption: (A) Ribo-Seq coverage reveals a non-annotated coding gene (LDHU3_36.4050). (B) Its conservation in other Leishmania species.

items.title: Structural determinants responsible for the preferential insertion of ribonucleotides by bacterial NHEJ poldom
items.description: First author. Outcome of my Microbiology Master's thesis on bacterial DNA repair.
items.summary: The polymerization domain (PolDom) of bacterial Ligase D repairs DNA double-strand breaks by non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) and prefers ribonucleotides (NTPs) over deoxynucleotides, which is key when the cell's dNTP pool is depleted. We biochemically analysed Pseudomonas aeruginosa PolDom variants at three conserved residues (His651, Ser768 and Lys606). The histidine is mainly responsible for the preference for ribonucleotides and for the plasticity of the active site, while Lys606 stabilises primer dislocations. PolDom also uses 8oxoGTP efficiently, a nucleotide lesion caused by oxidative stress.
highlights: His651 drives the preference for ribonucleotides.
Efficient insertion of 8oxoGMP in both its anti and syn conformations.
items.image_caption: Primer-extension kinetics of wild-type PolDom and its serine and histidine variants, with ribonucleotides versus deoxynucleotides.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: What data this website processes, why, and for how long. In short: no tracking or advertising cookies, no profiles, and IP addresses are not stored.

sections.title: Who is responsible
sections.body: Alejandro Sánchez Salvador, owner of asansal.com. Contact: asansal@outlook.es.

sections.title: Visit statistics
sections.body:
To understand how the site is used, I record anonymous events: the visit, the page language, the country (provided by Cloudflare), the type of device, the sections you open, clicks on links to other websites, CV downloads and the website you came from.

Each visitor gets an anonymous identifier calculated from the IP address and the browser together with a random key that changes every day and is deleted after two days. After that, nobody, including me, can link the identifier to an IP address. The IP address itself is never stored. These statistics are kept for up to 13 months.

sections.title: AI assistant
sections.body:
The questions you write to the assistant are sent to the Google Gemini API to generate the answer. This site uses Google's paid API, whose terms do not allow Google to use them to train its models.

I also store the text of each question, with its language, its topic and the anonymous identifier, to see what visitors want to know and to improve the assistant. Please do not include personal data in your questions. Questions are kept for up to 13 months.

sections.title: Protection against abuse
sections.body: To prevent automated abuse of the assistant, the number of questions per day is counted with an anonymous identifier derived from the IP address, which is deleted after two days. After 5 questions, Cloudflare Turnstile may ask you to confirm that you are not a robot. Cloudflare processes the data needed for that check under its own privacy policy.

sections.title: Hosting and security
sections.body: The site is served through Cloudflare, which protects it against attacks and bots and, to do so, processes technical data such as your IP address. The server is hosted on Oracle Cloud. Like any web server, it may keep technical access logs, including IP addresses, for a limited time for security purposes.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: This site does not use tracking or advertising cookies. Cloudflare may set strictly necessary security cookies, for example to tell people and bots apart.

sections.title: External content
sections.body: Fonts and icons are served from this server, without contacting Google. The Tableau section loads previews and dashboards from Tableau Public (Salesforce), which receives your IP address when you open that section. Links to other websites (LinkedIn, GitHub, scientific journals, Sextant IA, lab.asansal.com) are governed by their own privacy policies.

sections.title: Legal basis
sections.body: Statistics, security, abuse protection and answering the questions you send to the assistant are based on legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR): knowing how the site is used and keeping it safe, with data that do not identify you.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can request access to your data, its rectification or erasure, or object to its processing, by writing to asansal@outlook.es. As the data are anonymous, I may need details to find them, for example the exact text and date of a question. You can also lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (www.aepd.es).
